documented_probe: nltk/nltk @ parent c86229d218978628eb4e6e100ff266d2a939b7f0 (bug present; fix commit 1929bf9e365faa9e476b3abbccb72a74351d647e, issue #3687 closing #1995). Shallow clone + golden-test extraction in a throwaway clone. Image builds in ~15-25 s at 1 CPU (pure-Python project; the venv re-install of the pristine tree dominates). Reproduces in <1 s: NLTKWordTokenizer().tokenize("'hello'") -> ["'hello", "'"] (opening quote glued) and tokenize("'tis a fine day'") -> ["'t", 'is', 'a', 'fine', 'day', "'"] (word split); word_tokenize("'Hard' to tell") -> ["'Hard", "'", 'to', 'tell']. Fixed tree returns ["'", 'hello', "'"], ["'", 'tis', ...], ["'", 'Hard', "'", 'to', 'tell'] and keeps o'clock / O'Connor intact; the project's regression test then passes. The verifier runs the agent's own /app/reproduce.py against a pristine non-editable install of the parent tree (/opt/venv) expecting failure, then against an overlay containing only the agent's tokenizer source expecting success, plus the fix-commit golden test, the full parent tokenize suite (78 passed pre- and post-fix), and 3 authored hidden cases.
notes: Upstream-clone debugging task (v4.2 family): nltk/nltk at the parent of the fix for issue #3687, where NLTKWordTokenizer pads an opening single quote only when the following word is exactly one letter long (the old rule used a (\w)\b capture), so quoted multi-letter words keep the quote glued ('hello -> "'hello) and a few short forms get split mid-word ('tis -> "'t' + 'is'). The checkout is cloned shallow at the parent commit (fix commit never in the object store; golden extraction happens in a throwaway clone that is deleted). The instruction describes the user-visible symptom (glued opening quotes, mid-word splits, clitics/o'clock must stay intact) and names neither the issue, the commit, the source file nor the fix; it requires the agent to write its own reproduction (/app/reproduce.py) as a deliverable, which must fail on the pre-fix code and pass on the repaired code. The verifier (a) pins /usr/local (interpreter + site-packages) and /app/src (allowing only nltk/tokenize/destructive.py to differ; .git/info/exclude hashed) and /opt/golden (SHA-256) to build-time manifests under tests/manifests, blocking sitecustomize/.pth/interpreter wrappers, pip-install upgrades at trial time and golden-test edits; (b) asserts provenance: HEAD still the parent, only destructive.py modified, no strays, fix commit unreachable (git cat-file -e); (c) runs the agent's reproduction against a pristine non-editable install of the parent tree in /opt/venv (must FAIL) and against an overlay of that tree with only the agent's destructive.py (must PASS), plus the same reproduction against the repaired /app/src itself; (d) runs the project's own regression test extracted from the fix commit (test_word_tokenize_opening_single_quote_padding, via word_tokenize with seeded punkt_tab); (e) runs the project's own full tokenizer unit suite at /app/src (78 passed, 2 skipped) to prove nothing else broke; (f) runs three authored hidden cases exercising the quote-padding code path from inputs the upstream test does not use: capitalized quoted words ('Twas, 'Bout, 'goodbye), contraction/intra-word apostrophe preservation with quoted words (dog's 'bark', don't 'worry' 'bout it, 'she's here', 'don't' stop, isn't), and the punkt-based word_tokenize path ('Really?', 'quality' over 'quantity'). The nltk editable install's PEP 660 finder maps 'nltk' to /app/src, so no PYTHONPATH game can smuggle a fix outside the one allowed source file; a pip-installed released nltk would alter /usr/local and fail the manifest. Reward is binary with the standard trap.
